description.en: Roughly 90 km coastal route from Tanabe to Nachi via Kushimoto, rounding Cape Shionomisaki at the southern tip of the Kii Peninsula — the shoreline route, rather than the mountain passes of the Nakahechi and Kohechi. This release ships it as a metadata stub only: OpenStreetMap holds no route relation for the Ōhechi at all, so there is no walked line to package yet. See the osm block below for what the corridor sweep found.

distanceNote.en: 90 km and about four days are the scoping figures this pilgrimage's own design spec sets for the Ōhechi (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-05-pilgrimages-and-sections-design.md, section 5.2) — not measured against a walked line, because none exists yet and OSM does not yet hold enough of this trail to build one. Expect this figure to be corrected once the section is cut.

sources.notes: A relation sweep of the Tanabe to Kushimoto to Nachi corridor found no Ōhechi route relation — see the osm block below. No geometry ships from this source this release.

osm.note: No relation exists. A sweep of every route/hiking/foot/pilgrimage relation in the Tanabe → Kushimoto → Nachi corridor returned seven relations, and all seven are Nakahechi or Kohechi — nothing named or tagged for the Ōhechi. The trail exists in OpenStreetMap only as five loose, unrelated ways clustered inside Tanabe, 0.58 km in total: way 298987443 (name:en="Kumano Kodo Ohechi Route") plus four unnamed neighbours (300025709, 300025708, 129180109, 129185848). No relation id is recorded here because none exists; inventing one, or pinning a neighbouring route's relation, would misrepresent what OSM holds. ways: null until a route relation is created upstream.
